title: Introduce change-aware CI orchestrator, prebuild cache, and dependency grouping
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce a change-aware presubmit orchestration that reduces CI runtime and queue pressure; add a cross-runner prebuild cache; group Dependabot updates by ecosystem for clearer dependency review; remove legacy Makefile entrypoints.
description: Context: Our presubmit lanes run a largely monolithic set of linters and integration tests which causes long queue times and redundant work across PRs that touch a small subset of packages. This PR implements a change-aware CI orchestrator that computes the minimal set of lint/test targets based on a lightweight path-to-package map, plus a short smoke prober and a cross-runner prebuild cache to reduce duplicated setup time. Goals: reduce median presubmit runtime, lower CI cost, and improve signal-to-noise for reviewers. Key design points: 1) change-aware orchestrator: a tiny service (TS script) invoked in the presubmit entrypoint that inspects git diff against main and maps changed paths -> package/test matrix; the mapping is configurable via .ci/package-map.json; 2) smoke prober lane: a 30–60s quick check that runs critical smoke tests (server start, API health, schema validation) to provide fast feedback; failures block merges and route developers to the full lanes; 3) prebuild cache: store shared prebuilt artifacts (node_modules bundles, pip wheel cache, rust target dir) in an S3-backed cache keyed by toolchain hash and package set so parallel runners can rehydrate quickly; 4) typed action conversion: replace fragile shell composite actions used for setup with a small TypeScript action to reduce flakiness and make input validation explicit; 5) dependency grouping: adjust .github/dependabot.yml to group infra (actions/tooling) separately from runtime deps and enable security-only updates on infra groups; 6) repo hygiene: remove legacy Makefiles (Makefile.dev, Makefile.ci) and centralize entrypoints under scripts/ci-bootstrap and toolchain.json. Checklist: - [x] Implement change-aware orchestrator script and package-map defaults - [x] Add smoke-prober lane and gating policy - [x] Add prebuild cache implementation and infra docs - [x] Convert two composite actions (ci-setup, cache-warm) to TypeScript actions - [x] Update dependabot config and add grouping rules - [x] Remove legacy makefiles and update docs/ci.md - [x] Add e2e harness toggles for full-presubmit vs. targeted-presubmit - [x] Add rollout plan + canary (50% of PRs will use new orchestrator for 48h) Migration notes: - The package-map can originate from repo metadata (workspaces) or be manually curated for edge cases. - There is a feature flag in .github/ci-flags.json to opt a repository subgroup into the new orchestrator; rollout used this flag to avoid global blast radius. - Owners: infra (Asha), platform (Diego), dx (Linnea). Motivation and numbers: Early internal canary reduced median presubmit time from ~14m to ~5m for small PRs touching a single package and reduced runner-hours by ~34% over two weeks. We observed a small class of false-negatives for path-only format changes (docs affecting generated code) which we addressed by expanding the package-map and adding a docs->schema mapping. Risks and mitigations: - Missing mapped packages -> fallback to full-presubmit (safe). - Cache key collisions -> include toolchain and package manifest fingerprints. - Action rewrite regressions -> small TS actions have unit tests and are published pinned in the manifest. Impact: CI queue times and billable runner-minutes reduced; faster feedback loop for engineers; clearer dependency update PRs via grouping.

review_comments:
Diego Morales: Can the orchestrator handle cross-package integration tests that require multiple packages?
Asha Patel: Yes — the package-map supports grouping keys and an explicit 'integration: true' tag that forces the orchestrator to include related packages; we also fallback to the full-presubmit if an integration tag is present.
Linnea Berg: The TS actions look cleaner but please ensure we pin node versions and add unit tests for action inputs.
Asha Patel: Added unit tests under tests/actions and we pin node in action.yml to 20.x.
Omar Khan: How do we prevent Dependabot from creating a noisy series of PRs for infra actions?
Asha Patel: We added grouping and a security-only toggle for infra; we also set weekly cadence for infra bundles and daily for runtime security patches.
Linnea Berg (approval): Left a couple of nits on docs phrasing but overall LGTM.
Diego Morales (approval): Verified rollout metrics from canary and approves merge.
